text: Gold and silver trade in choppy ranges after an extreme one-day drawdown. Silver slips about 0.3% near $78.70 after a 28% drop; gold falls roughly 3% near $4,707 after nearly 10% down Friday. CME raises COMEX margin requirements to 8% for gold and 15% for 5,000-oz silver. The dollar index is ~0.8% higher since Thursday; WTI crude is ~4% lower. Metals oscillate intraday without settling into a stable band.

meta.note: Boundary blur between macro pricing signals and market plumbing created channel tension.

text: Fiscal Q1 results show Experiences as the profit core ($3.31B operating income, +6% YoY; $10B+ revenue), while Entertainment weaknes ($1.1B operating income, -35% YoY). Total revenue ~$26B (+5% YoY); adjusted EPS $1.63. Streaming revenue $5.35B (+11%) with projected ~500M operating income next quarter. Sports revenue +1% but margins squeezed by higher rights costs and cord-cutting. Shares fall ~7% on release as reporting granularity contracts (no subscriber counts, fewer linear disclosures).

meta.note: Boundary blue between Corporate and Media Infrastructure classifications.

text: The United States and India finalize a trade deal after a bilateral phone call. The U.S. lowers its reciprocal tariff on Indian imports to approximately 18% from prior levels, while India agrees to eliminate tariffs and non-tariff barriers against U.S. goods and commit to substantial increased purchases of U.S. energy, technology, agriculture, and other products. As part of the broader framework, India's purchases of Russian oil are reported to decline. The agreement takes immediate effect.

meta.note: Clarity on penal tariff removal versus base tariff reduction remains ambiguous in available reports.

text: The Bureau of Labor Statistics will not release the January Employment Situation report on Feb. 6 because federal funding has lapsed. Other routine BLS releases (including JOLTS, CPI, and trade data) remain at risk of delay. The government closed Saturday after Congress failed to pass a spending plan; timing of funding resumption is uncertain. Markets had been positioned around an expected +55,000 payroll print and 4.4% unemployment.

meta.note: Boundary friction between Governance and Macro-Economy channels.

text: SpaceX becomes the managing member of X.AI Holdings as the two firms are legally combined in Nevada. The merged structure links launch, Starlink connectivity, social platform data, and AI compute under one ownership envelope while positioning for a reported $1.25T public listing. Capital flows consolidate around a single Musk-controlled architecture even as xAI remains cash-intensive and infrastructure-constrained.

meta.note: Tension between commercial consolidation and unresolved regulatory exposure.

text: Q4 results exceed expectations as U.S. government and commercial demand concenrate around Palantir's AI software stack. Revenue reaches $1.41B with 70% YoY growth; U.S. government up 66% and U.S. commercial more than doubles. Net income rises sharply to $608M. Forward guidance for 2026 materially exceeds analyst baselines, even as shares had been down ~15% year-to-date before the after-hours move.

meta.note: Tensino between earnings strength and prior market repricing could not be resolved cleanly into a single vector.
